body:
> Observed 2026-08-29 04:43 on hkb's own board, with the fix from #153 (PR #160) on main. `hkb request-changes 185` (another process) added the synthetic `changes_requested` row at 04:42:21 and set the card `ready`; the loop's next tick at 04:43:26 logged `#185: open PR #190 → review (active_pr guard)` — the exact bounce #153 removed. `activePrGuard(attempts, prs)` on the live data answers `guard: false, continues: true`; the tick answered `guard: true` because it judged attempts **without** that row.

## Why

`listComments` (`src/tasks.js` ~144) memoises `comments:<n>` in `ctx._cache`, and `saveRun` invalidates it only for writes made by the same process (~172). `loop()` (`src/dispatch.js` ~989) reuses one `ctx` for every tick and clears `ctx._cache` only on the self-heal `drop_caches` path (~415). So the first `loadRun(n)` a loop ever makes for a card — here at 04:33, when it stopped #185's idle agent — is the run record it will believe until it restarts. `src/mcp.js` ~286 already clears the cache per call with the comment "a server outlives many calls; never answer from a previous call's comments"; the loop has the identical hazard and never got the same line.

Consequences beyond tonight's bounce: any verb run outside the loop process — a worker's `finish`/`block`/`request-review`, an operator's `request-changes`/`unblock`, the Actions dispatcher's writes — is invisible to a running loop for any card it has already touched. Which paths that corrupts depends on what `reconcile`/`reap`/the guard read from `loadRun` (~268, ~536, ~632, ~700, ~785). The bounce is the visible one; audit the others.

## What

1. **Scope the comments cache to one tick** (`src/dispatch.js` `tick` entry, or `loop` before each `tick`): `ctx._cache = { ...keep the parts that are per-process by design (`base`, `mergeGate`), comments: fresh }` — the way `mcp.js` does it. Cheapest correct fix. Alternatively key the memo on the issue's `updated_at` from the board read the tick already has (`fetchBoard` returns it): a hit only when the issue has not changed since the cache was filled — that keeps the read-saving for untouched cards and is provably fresh for the rest.
2. **Test** (`test/dispatch.test.js`, fake-gh): tick 1 loads #n's run; between ticks the fake-gh store gains a `changes_requested` row written "by another process"; tick 2 claims the continuation instead of guarding. A second test for a worker's `finish` between ticks being seen by reconcile.
3. Audit note in the PR: which tick paths read `loadRun` and what a stale record did to each (protocol_violation write-offs? reclaim? the active_pr guard?).

## Done when

- The fake-gh two-tick test passes; `hkb request-changes <n>` from another process is honoured by the next tick of a loop that had already loaded the card.
- `npm run lint && npm test` green.

## Contract

- Keep the memo within a tick (many reads of one card per tick are the frugal case it exists for); do not add API calls for cards the tick does not touch.
goal: A tick never judges a card on comments cached by an earlier tick: the per-process comments cache is scoped to one tick (or keyed on the issue's updated_at the board read already carries), so request-changes, finish and block written from other processes are seen on the next tick
title: The dispatcher loop caches every card's comments for its whole lifetime, so a run record written by any other process — request-changes, a worker's finish or block — is invisible to it
